tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

bermejo-core-idea-cost-as-coordinate: Sec. II, p.2: the paper states its own method in one sentence (cost as an extra coordinate) and defines it in II.A and II.B
bermejo-aim-escape-plateaus-not-lower-co: Sec. I, p.1: the authors state their approach aims to leave barren plateaus, not to lower cost values
bermejo-option1-hyperspherical: Sec. II.A, p.2: steps 1 to 3 define the hyperspherical option, including the projection back to the cost function
bermejo-option2-plane-rotation: Sec. II.B, p.2-3: the paper defines the frame rotation, and says the angle may be an extra hyperparameter, as in most of its results
bermejo-apply-only-at-plateaus-option: Sec. II.A, p.2: the paper states the transform can be applied only at minima or plateaus or alternated with the original; Sec. II.B repeats it
bermejo-learning-rate-retuning: Sec. II, p.4: the authors state that scales change in the new coordinates and the old learning rate may fail; their closing remark is phrased as an expectation, not a measured result
bermejo-benchmark-setup-pennylane: Sec. III, p.4: the paper states its protocol (PennyLane originals, most efficient optimizer, mostly Adam). 'Optimal and fine-tuned' is their description of the baselines, not shown
bermejo-limit-untested-deep-learning: Sec. IV, p.8: the authors say the method must still be tested on CNNs, transformers and generative models
lemma1-p-gate-second-moment: Lemma 1, App. A.2, p.19-20: stated with its conditions (independent 2-designs over U(4)) and proved from the two-fold commutant of U(4); the 2/5 coefficients follow from projecting |is> onto span{|ii>,|ss>}
definition-bodyness: Sec. III.A, p.5: the paper defines bodyness as the number of qubits a Pauli acts on non-trivially
definition-k-purity: App. A.1, p.18: k-purity defined as the projection onto Paulis of bodyness k, Eq. (A1)
locally-easy-necessary-not-sufficient: Sec. III.B, p.6: the authors state a locally-easy dataset is necessary but not sufficient for the optimization to stay in the low-bodyness subspace
result1-average-case-only: Sec. III.A, p.6: the authors state Result 1 holds only on average for random initialization and that their numerics are a heuristic extension, not a bridge to worst case
entanglement-caveat-guarantees-void: Sec. III.A, p.5-6: the authors state the guarantees fail when input data are too entangled (volume law)
definition-classical-simulability-with-s: Sec. II.B, p.4-5: the paper states the definition of classical simulability it adopts (following Ref. [49])
definition-dequantized-no-circuit-on-dev: Sec. II.B, p.5: the paper defines 'dequantized' and says its approach is a substantial but not full dequantization
variance-tracing-out-leq-measurement-bas: Eq. (7), Sec. III.C and App. E.1, Eq. (E8)-(E12), p.31-32: derived from positivity of overlaps with identity/swap strings, under independent 2-designs in the convolutional layer, with the zero-mean check for E[N]
setup-qcnn-definition-tracing-out-and-me: Sec. II.A, p.3-4: the paper states the two QCNN variants it studies, the log depth and the O(1)-qubit observable
setup-quantum-datasets-and-training: Sec. IV.A, p.7: DMRG ground states, Pauli shadows, 15-parameter two-qubit blocks, cross-entropy loss and LBFGS are all stated as written
surrogate-trained-to-solve-not-emulate: Sec. IV.A, p.7: the authors state the surrogate is trained to solve the tasks, not to emulate an exact QCNN's training
setup-classical-datasets-and-encodings: Sec. IV.B, p.10-11: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, EuroSAT, GTSRB, 8-qubit MPS amplitude encoding, three angle encodings, MSE loss; Table I caption
pauli-propagation-surrogate-method: App. B.1.b, p.25-26: the paper describes its LOWESA variant and the four truncations (bodyness, frequency, sliding window, variance)
tensor-network-method-three-steps: App. B.2, p.26-27: the three steps are described, with the third optional for classification
tensor-network-method-limits-binary-1d: App. B.2, p.26: the authors state the method is binary-only and best in 1D, with the rest left to future work
discussion-scope-1d-architectures-only: Sec. V, p.12: the authors state they simulate only 1D tracing out and measurement-based QCNNs and did not pursue 2D or exotic topologies
open-question-positive-bias-or-physical-: Sec. V, p.13: the authors leave the positive-bias versus physical-phenomenon question open
measurement-qcnn-example-uses-brick-arch: App. E.2, p.32: brick-like two-qubit gates, measurement in the pooling layer controlling a single-qubit unitary on a neighbour
qcnn-no-full-dequantization: Sec. V, p.11-12: the authors state they do not prove no QCNN is ever needed and that their claims are not a full dequantization. The 'burden of proof' clause is their stance, not a result; the team lead may split it
a-qgan-anomaly-score-definition: Sec. II B 2, Eq. (9)-(10), p.4: the paper defines the score as a weighted sum of a residual (fidelity) term and a discriminator term, with threshold delta
fidelity-exponential-concentration-open: Sec. II B 2, p.4: the authors flag that their fidelity term can suffer exponential concentration (citing [50,51]) and that scalable distances are open; a caveat on their own score
threshold-set-with-bsm-data: Sec. II B 1, p.3: the authors state how delta is chosen, using SM and BSM training data for a baseline
alpha-grid-search-on-test-auc: Sec. III D, p.5: the authors state the alpha grid search on test AUC and the mean-score thresholds
dataset-sizes-and-features: Sec. III A, p.4: the event counts (3,450,279; 3,450,277; 139,991; 6,910) and 23 features are stated as written
artificial-simulated-hep-data: Sec. III A, p.4: the authors state the data are artificial and the BSM sets are simulated with PYTHIA8
quantum-sample-sizes-100-versus-classica: Sec. III A, p.4-5: 100 events per set for the quantum case; the classical case uses 1000 including those 100
pca-compression-and-angle-encoding: Sec. III A, p.5: PCA compression, normalization to [-pi/2, pi/2] and angle encoding (Eq. 11) are stated
ten-random-instances-3-to-8-features: Sec. IV A, p.6: 10 random instances and 3 to 8 PCA features are stated
classical-benchmark-parameter-matched: Sec. IV A, p.6: the authors state the classical nets are built with a comparable number of trainable parameters
discriminator-updates-more-than-generato: Sec. IV A, p.6: 5 times more discriminator updates for 3 features and 10 times for 7 features
simulation-training-settings: Sec. IV A, p.6: noiseless run 500 epochs with AMSGRAD (lr 1e-3, betas given); noisy run same optimizer, lr 1e-2, ten times fewer epochs
effective-dimension-definition: Sec. III E, p.5: the paper describes the effective dimension it uses (from Ref. [33]) as a measure of coverable model space, higher meaning higher capacity
effective-dimension-directly-comparable: Sec. IV C, p.7 and Fig. 7 caption: the authors state equal or similar trainable parameter counts, so they compare effective dimensions directly; the comparison basis is their own setup
larger-scale-experiments-infeasible: Sec. IV, p.6: the authors state larger-scale experiments are infeasible with current noise; runs use up to 8 features in simulation and 3 on hardware
results-preliminary-future-work: Sec. V, p.8: the authors call their results preliminary and name more data sets and larger sizes as future work
lack-of-data-not-typical-problem: Sec. V, p.8: the authors caution that lack of data is typically not a problem in this HEP task, which limits the weight of their ten-times-fewer-samples result
scope-overview-no-method: Sec. 1, p.2: the authors state the paper is an overview of opportunities and challenges, with no new method
p5-definition: Sec. 1, p.2: the paper defines P5 medicine by its five terms (citing [22]) and uses the term throughout
future-work-ethics: Sec. 4, p.17: the authors state future work (overcoming challenges, implementing the concepts, ethics)
qml-four-types-definition: Sec. 1.2.4, p.9-10 and Fig. 3: the paper lays out CC, QC, CQ and QQ with their meanings
bertl-review-scope: Sec. 2, p.10: the authors state that the following subsections summarize current research on QC advantages in P5 medicine
nora-architecture-definition: Fig. 1 caption and Sec. 2.1, p.3: layers, ancillary thermal qudits in |0> and non-locality are defined as written
nora-nonlocal-generalization-of-mera: Sec. 1, p.1 and abstract: the authors define NoRA as the MERA family with locality removed
nora-scaling-specialization-scope: Sec. 2.2, p.3-4: the paper primarily treats n_l ~ k + r^l, with r = 2
nora-complexity-gate-count-estimate: Sec. 2.3, p.4: the paper defines its complexity estimate as the gate count (Eq. 5-6) and says it is only an upper bound
nora-toy-hamiltonian-definition: Sec. 2.4, p.4 and App. A.1: the toy Hamiltonian H = -sum J_i P_i has the network as an exact ground state and an exactly degenerate ground space
nora-toy-hamiltonian-nonlocal: Sec. 2.4, p.4: the authors state the toy Hamiltonian is highly non-local, limiting physical interpretation
nora-clifford-code-interpretation: Sec. 3, p.6: the paper states that its Clifford version is read as an encoding circuit of a stabilizer code with ground state qudits as logical qudits (citing [41] for the standard fact)
nora-clifford-focus-reason: Sec. 3, p.5-6: the authors state they focus on the Clifford model because its properties can be classically simulated
nora-random-layer-definition: Sec. 3.2, p.6: random Clifford gates on randomly chosen non-intersecting q-sets per sublayer; the Trotterization reading is stated as heuristic
nora-code-distance-definition: Fig. 4 caption and Sec. 3.3.1, p.7-8: the distance is defined by vanishing mutual information with the reference
nora-distance-upper-bound-method: Sec. 3.3.1, p.8: the authors state the Monte Carlo method gives only an upper bound on the distance
nora-stabilizer-weight-definition: Sec. 3.3.2, p.8: weight and constant weight are defined
nora-numerical-scope-nonexhaustive: Sec. 4, p.8: the authors call the numerical analysis non-exhaustive
nora-numerical-setup: Sec. 4, p.8: Python 3.10.4, Numpy, Galois, any odd-prime-power dimension, 1000-sample averages, d = 3, r = 2, q = 2 are stated
nora-code-availability: Sec. 4, p.8: the code location and data-on-request terms are stated
nora-fixed-ground-space-rate: Sec. 4.1, p.8: with fixed k and N = k + r^L (Eq. 1-4), the rate k/N falls exponentially in L. The step is immediate from the paper's own formulas, but the text gives no separate proof, so a reader may prefer low
nora-distance-computing-cost: Sec. 4.1.2, p.10: the authors state the cost grows exponentially in N, so larger systems are hard to study
nora-ground-space-scaling-setup: Sec. 4.2, p.12-13: k = r^a, L = a + b, rate 1/(1+r^b) independent of a, thermodynamic limit a to infinity
nora-scaling-examples-parameters: Sec. 4.2, p.13: D = 3 and b = 1 for the examples
nora-scaling-open-items: Sec. 4.2.2, p.13-14: the authors state the trend is not yet shown for other g and r or larger a and b, and the phase transition is future work
nora-clifford-caution-not-syk: Sec. 5, p.14: the authors caution that the Clifford layer model is not right for the actual SYK model
nora-operator-growth-model: Sec. 5.1, p.14-15: the authors state the operator growth assumption of their distance estimate
nora-renyi-flat-spectrum: App. C.4, p.33 and footnote 15: stated for n > 0 with the flat-spectrum condition (rho_A proportional to a projection) and proved by direct trace in the footnote
nora-not-efficiently-contractible: Sec. 1, p.2 and Sec. 6.3, p.18: the authors state the networks are not efficiently contractible classically without added structure. They give no proof; the value is attributed correctly

theory_low.result1-tracing-out-exponential-decay: Result 1 is informal (Sec. III.A, p.5); the decay is read from a plot of the exact formula (Fig. 8, App. A.3), with no stated rate in Result 1 itself
theory_low.theorem1-exact-kpurity-formula: Theorem 1 and its derivation are in App. A.3 (pp.20-22), but Eq. (A17)/(A20) is unreadable in the text layer, so the value cannot say what is proved; the proof also rests on a path-counting derivation, not a short check
theory_low.result2-measurement-based-exponential-de: Result 2 is informal (Sec. III.C, p.6); App. E.1 gives an argument based on the q_j coefficients, not a stated and proved theorem
theory_low.measurement-qcnn-q-equals-one-pathologic: App. E.1, p.32: an informal argument about the q_j=1 case and tensor-network simulability, not a stated theorem
theory_low.pauli-propagation-exponential-path-growt: App. B.1.a, p.24: a standard property stated in one sentence ('can create'), argued informally from Eq. (B6); not a stated and proved result
theory_low.nora-power-law-entropy-derivation: App. A.3.2, Eq. (65)-(69), p.27-28 and Sec. 2.4: a low-temperature, continuum-limit approximation with an incomplete-gamma upper bound; the authors write 'could indeed' and confirm only by plots (Fig. 2, 14)
theory_low.nora-stabilizer-entropy-decouples: App. A.2, p.25: the decoupling is derived after 'ignoring that leading term', and the equations are garbled in the text layer, so the stored statement cannot carry its conditions
theory_low.nora-weight-growth-factor-heuristic: Sec. 4.1.2 and App. B, p.28-29: a heuristic estimate for the case w0 much less than n, with 'approximately' bounds; the link to code distance is only expected
theory_low.nora-dsat-estimate: Sec. 4.1.2, p.10: a heuristic estimate from Eq. (18), compared with simulation; not a proved result
theory_low.nora-singleton-relative-bound-third: Sec. 4.2.1, Eq. (23), p.13: arithmetic on the quantum Singleton bound, which the paper cites and does not prove here; an upper bound on distance, not an achieved value
theory_low.nora-syk-complexity-n-log-n: Sec. 5, Eq. (26) and Sec. 5.2, p.14-16: a gate-count estimate, only an upper bound on complexity, compared informally with holographic conjectures
theory_low.nora-distance-regimes: Sec. 5.1.1-5.1.2, p.15 and Sec. 5.3: an analytic estimate resting on the growth assumption; the authors write 'we expect' and 'could be'

value_replace.hardware-run-setup: The authors state that the hardware run trained on subsets of 50 events taken from the 10 training data sets, and used ten to the fourth shots (the text layer prints 104, a lost superscript) for each expectation value estimation during the training and the anomaly score computation.
